result:
`validateApp` now throws if `owner` is missing or empty, and all three apps pass an owner. PR #1 is merged, and CI and CD both came back green. I haven't opened the deployed apps, so "still starts up" rests on the three local builds, which compiled and passed the contract check. I marked all four child tickets done and closed the epic.

**PR:** #1 on the monorepo (`plat-103-require-owner`). It carries all the changes for tickets 1 to 3 in one PR. The shared contract is inlined into each app at build time, so landing it separately would have broken the apps at startup. Landing it alone also wouldn't have deployed anything, because CD only builds when something under `apps/` changes.

**Owners:** I picked the owner names myself, since nobody was available to ask. They are `platform-team` for core-shell and `billing-team` for billing and reports.

**Surprise:** `sub-route-reports` also calls `validateApp`, but no ticket covers it. I fixed it in the same PR, because otherwise it would have failed at startup once the contract changed. The epic's acceptance criteria cover every app that calls `validateApp`, so it was in scope.

**Slowdown:** My first `sed` edits failed on macOS and changed nothing, so I redid them with `perl`.
